about.title: Editing is the work. Scrubbing dead air isn't.
about.lede: A recurring podcast or interview show records for hours, then one producer spends hours more cutting what nobody wanted to hear. It is slow, repetitive, and not where the creator's judgment matters most. SudoCut removes that repetitive first pass.

one.title: Late is a cost too.
one.copy: An informational episode loses value every day it waits. Editing polish has no natural end point, so a show that chases it publishes less. Cutting the finishing time changes what gets published, not just what it costs.

two.title: The editor's taste is not the ground truth.
two.copy: Every other tool makes a human editor faster and asks the editor to approve the result. We are judged by the published episode instead. In our own tests producers were never satisfied with an edit they knew was AI-made — and the AI-edited uploads matched the human-edited ones on views anyway.

three.title: Nothing is a black box.
three.copy: Every cut can be inspected and put back. You get a Premiere or Final Cut project alongside the MP4, so the channel keeps control — as an option, not as a required human finishing pass.

proof.label: Editing time
proof.claim: One episode's editing time dropped to about one hour.
proof.detail: A full episode used to take about 4–6 hours to edit. With SudoCut, the rough cut and cleanup pass took about one hour. The human work stays. We reduce the repetitive cut cleanup so editors can focus on the parts that matter.
proof.tagline: Based on a channel we operate

team.title: Two founders. Both write the code.
team.lede: We met in June 2025 at the Hugging Face LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon in Seoul — Jong Hyun ran the Seoul site, Jiho competed in it. Both of us have been full-time on SudoCut since June 2026.

jonghyun.name: Jong Hyun Park
jonghyun.copy: Built the first prototypes, and runs the channel they are tested on — an AI podcast channel of 1.5 years, 10K+ subscribers and over a million views. Started SudoCut in January 2026 after trying the AI editing tools on the market and finishing none of an episode with them.

jiho.name: Jiho Yang
jiho.copy:
Built products at several startups.
Studied mathematics at HKUST, and now builds SudoCut full-time.
Usually replies to work-related messages within 30 minutes.

one.title: We are not artists.
one.copy: There is art in editing. Our part of it isn't the art. We remove a chore so the creator's part can start sooner, and we don't confuse the two.

two.title: Direction over perfection.
two.copy: A cut that ships this week beats a perfect pipeline next year. We pick a direction, move, and let real footage correct us.

three.title: Honesty over polish.
three.copy: If the cut is wrong, we say it's wrong. Demos show real footage and real numbers, including the ones that don't flatter us.

four.title: AI proposes, humans decide.
four.copy: Every cut SudoCut makes is a suggestion on a timeline the creator still owns. The moment the tool decides instead of proposing, we've built the wrong product.

team.note: We are two. Jinho Kim produces the YouTube channel and Jiyun Lee, a professional video creator, advises on editing — neither has written product code, and neither is listed here because that is their call to make, not ours.
